question: Why must a nurse wash and clean instruments physically before using a disinfectant?
explanation: Think of it like washing dishes before putting them in the sterilizer! Cleaning washes away blood and dirt that can hide germs and stop the disinfectant from working properly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: You are getting surgical tools ready that will go deep inside sterile body tissues. What process do these instruments need?
explanation: Spot on! Anything entering sterile tissue or blood vessels must be 100% free of all germs, which means full sterilization is a must. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which level of cleaning is needed for reusable flexible endoscopes used in clinic?
explanation: Endoscopes touch mucous membranes (semi-critical items), so they need high-level disinfection to keep patients safe from stubborn germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: A blood pressure cuff is used over unbroken patient skin. What level of cleaning does it need?
explanation: Since it only touches intact skin, it's a non-critical item. Low-level disinfection is totally enough here! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: How do alcohol-based sprays and rubs mostly kill germs on surfaces?
explanation: Alcohol acts fast by breaking down and destroying the proteins inside microbial cells, stopping them in their tracks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: Isopropyl alcohol dries up very quickly on surfaces. Why can this sometimes be a problem when disinfecting?

options.A: It increases the corrosiveness of the metal
options.B: It leaves behind a sticky chemical residue
options.C: It causes severe skin burns in patients
options.D: It reduces the required wet contact time

explanation: Disinfectants need to stay wet on a surface for a set time to do their job. If the alcohol dries up too fast, it might not kill everything! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: What happens if a dirty instrument covered in blood or tissue is put straight into a disinfectant without washing first?

options.A: It accelerates the action of bleach
options.C: It shields microbes from the chemical
options.D: It lowers the pH of the disinfectant

explanation: Leftover body fluids form a protective shield around germs, blocking the disinfectant from touching and killing them. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h4)

question: A nurse wipes a table with disinfectant and immediately dries it off with a towel. What is the most likely result?

options.A: Inadequate microbial destruction due to lost contact time
options.B: Enhanced chemical penetration through the cell wall
options.C: Complete sterilization of the treatment surface
options.D: Rapid neutralization of toxic chemical fumes

explanation: Don't rush the drying! Disinfectants need to sit wet on the surface for a few minutes to successfully destroy all the germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the golden rule for the physical direction when wiping down a hospital bedside table?

options.A: From the bottom to the top
options.B: From dirty areas to clean areas
options.D: From clean areas to dirty areas

explanation: Always move from clean to dirty! That way, you don't drag germs back onto the parts of the table you just finished cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is guessing or eye-balling chemical mixtures a bad idea when preparing disinfectants?

options.A: It changes the color of the plastic container
options.B: It can render the solution ineffective or unsafe
options.C: It increases the evaporation rate of the fluid
options.D: It leaves a powdery residue on clinical surfaces

explanation: Always measure accurately! Too weak won't kill germs, and too strong can harm your patients, damage equipment, or hurt your skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h5)

question: If there is an accidental chemical splash in the ward, where should a nurse quickly look for safety and first-aid instructions?
explanation: Every clinical chemical has an SDS (Safety Data Sheet). It's your go-to guide for hazards, handling tips, and what to do in an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)

question: A nurse is pouring a strong chemical disinfectant into an open basin in a small utility room. What main hazard needs to be watched out for?

options.A: Electrical shock from the plumbing pipes

explanation: Strong solutions like glutaraldehyde give off sharp fumes. Always make sure the room is well-ventilated and protect your airways! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)
